entities.summary: Aryabhata (b. 476 CE, Pataliputra) was a renowned astronomer, mathematician, and engineer of the Classical era, whose groundbreaking contributions to trigonometry, algebra, and geocentric model of the universe had a lasting impact on Indian and later European mathematics and astronomy. His most notable work, the Aryabhatiya, introduced the concept of zero and the decimal system, revolutionizing mathematical notation and calculation. Aryabhata's significance extends beyond his scientific achievements, as his work influenced the development of astronomy and mathematics in ancient India and later in the Islamic Golden Age and Europe. The Aryabhatiya was a foundational text in the Indian mathematical tradition, and its impact can still be seen in modern mathematics and science. The astronomer's most famous prediction, the arrival of the moon at the vernal equinox, remained unfulfilled for centuries until its rediscovery in the 20th century. Aryabhata's legacy has been rediscovered in recent years, and his work continues to inspire new generations of scientists and mathematicians.
